AUTOMATIC1111 is a web interface for AI image generation, built with Gradio.

Here are the examples of server URLs:
• http://192.168.0.2:%1$s
• http://yourdomain.com:%1$s
• https://yourdomain.com

This mode allows you to test the application behavior, even if you don\'t have an AUTOMATIC1111 WebUI server.\n\nIn demo mode app ignores user prompt, does not use AI server, and returns some mock images.

Before connecting ensure that:
• you are running AUTOMATIC1111 WebUI with flags --api --listen
• your firewall is not blocking 7860 port
• phone is on the same WiFi with your PC
Before connecting ensure that:\n• your firewall is not blocking 7801 port\n• phone is on the same WiFi with your PC
Horde AI is a crowdsourced distributed cluster of Image generation workers and text generation workers.
You can use default API Key to connect anonymously. However anonymous accounts have the lowest priority when there\'s too many concurrent requests.
Hugging Face inference cloud provides a service that allows to test and evaluate publicly accessible machine learning models, or your own private models, for free.
OpenAI service allows image generation with GPT Image models.
Fal.ai provides hosted image generation model APIs with queue-based inference.
ArliAI provides SDNext-compatible cloud image generation APIs.
StabilityAI is the image generation service provided by DreamStudio.
A modular web interface for AI image generation, with an emphasis on accessible tools, high performance, and extensibility.
This configuration uses the Microsoft ONNX runtime to generate images on your phone, with no need to connect to a remote server or cloud.

Warning! Local Diffusion functionality is in beta-test. Don\'t expect for high quality images using local mode. \n\nThis implementation may not work well on non-powerful phones. Generation performance and speed depends on your phone resources (CPU, RAM) and the size of generated image (the smaller the image size, the faster the generation).
This configuration uses Google AI MediaPipe to generate images on your phone, with no need to connect to a remote server or cloud.
This configuration uses stable-diffusion.cpp and allows to run SDXL, SDXL-Turbo, LCM, or quantized GGUF models on your phone.

Exchange the output width and height, for example 768×512 becomes 512×768. This changes the output shape while keeping the input image intact.
Choose an output shape such as square, portrait or landscape. The form adjusts width and height to match the chosen ratio.
A LoRA is a small trained model add-on that helps draw a particular style, character or subject. Choose compatible LoRAs installed on your server and adjust their influence in the prompt.
Textual inversion creates an embedding: a learned shortcut word for a style or concept. Add an embedding from your server to the positive or negative prompt to guide what the model draws or avoids.
A hypernetwork is a small trained network that changes how a compatible model responds to your prompt, often to influence style. Choose one installed on your server and adjust its strength.

Create images from the current prompt, input image when used, and generation options. The selected provider runs the AI model. Remote providers receive these inputs and may use credits. Demo mode returns sample images instead. Tapping starts the task.
Choose several gallery images to export, delete, like or blur together. Tapping an image selects it instead of opening its details until you leave selection mode.

Open the server setup guide in your browser. It explains how to enable the server API so SDAI can connect.
On previews the app using sample images. It ignores your prompt and does not run AI generation. Off uses your own server address for real generation.
On uses AI Horde’s shared anonymous key. Off lets you enter your own account key. Requests using the anonymous key may have lower priority.
Open this provider’s website in your browser to learn about its image service and account requirements.
Open AI Horde’s registration page in your browser to create an account and obtain your own API key.
On lets you choose your own compatible model files. Off shows catalog models. Your original custom model files stay in their chosen folder.

Demo mode lets you explore SDAI using sample images. It does not create new images from your prompt, so the pictures will not match what you type.\n\nFor real generation with AUTOMATIC1111, you need a running AUTOMATIC1111 WebUI server: a program on your computer or another host that runs the image model. Turn Demo mode off and enter that server’s address. You can also choose a different provider in Set provider.
